# Svc::FatalHandler

## Overview {.unnumbered .unlisted}

`Svc::FatalHandler` is an F' system-service component that receives fatal conditions and applies the deployment's terminal fatal-response policy. It is placed in the Level 4 system-services and control layer because its response is satellite-wide rather than specific to one hardware subsystem.

## HuskySat-2 Use {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Hardware managers remain responsible for detecting device-specific failures and reporting them through typed events. `Svc::FatalHandler` has an application-facing command port for each Level 3 application. When it receives a fatal notification, it uses the appropriate port to send an application command carrying the fatal condition to the owning application. A hardware-related fatal event carries a unique opcode identifying the affected hardware; the application maps that opcode to the appropriate manager and issues that manager's reset command. This preserves the App-Manager-Driver boundary: the application decides what recovery action is appropriate, the manager owns the device-specific reset sequence, and the driver only exposes the low-level interface.

`Svc::FatalHandler` will remain the final system-level path for unhandled or escalated fatal conditions. It does not replace a hardware manager or become a central hardware-reset owner. If an event cannot be mapped safely to an owning application or hardware opcode, the deployment will escalate it to the terminal fatal-response policy.

### Proposed Hardware-Fault Pipeline {.unnumbered .unlisted}

The following is a proposed event and recovery flow. The exact event ports, opcode type, and escalation thresholds are TBR.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    M["Hardware manager detects fault"] --> E["Hardware fatal event<br/>unique hardware opcode"]
    E --> EM["Svc::EventManager<br/>event routing and filtering"]
    EM --> FHC["Svc::FatalHandler<br/>application-facing command port"]
    FHC --> A["Owning Level 3 application<br/>interprets opcode"]
    A --> C["Targeted reset command<br/>to selected manager"]
    C --> M
    FHC -. unhandled or escalated .-> F["Terminal fatal-response policy"]
```

This design keeps reset authority with the application-manager path while giving the system a defined terminal response when targeted recovery is unsafe or unavailable. The opcode namespace will be centrally documented so that every hardware manager emits unique, stable identifiers.
